# Preview your outputs

No own-study figures are displayed until you run and verify your inputs. Use the [synthetic](../synthetic/01-see-the-result.qmd) and [GLGC](../real-study/01-see-the-result.qmd) previews to learn what each plot can answer.

| Figure | Question | Important limit |
|---|---|---|
| Manhattan | Where are source associations concentrated? | Nearby variants can be correlated |
| Q–Q | How does the distribution compare with a reference? | Genome-wide background is required |
| Effect forest | What are direction, units and nominal intervals? | Top rows are selected and may be nearby |
| Frequency/INFO | Which values support filtering? | Frequency basis and missing scores matter |
| Effect-frequency | What patterns accompany frequency and effect? | Display and source selection affect the picture |
| N / precision | How does reported support relate to SE? | N and frequency do not fully explain the model |
| Filtering audit | What was excluded and why? | Source preparation and analysis are different stages |
| P consistency | Does beta/SE reproduce a particular normal calculation? | The source may use another test |
| Position zoom | What lies around the smallest retained p-value? | Position alone supplies neither LD nor genes |

The engine keeps all rows for calculations and thins only dense scatter backgrounds when needed. Use `scatter-display.tsv` to identify the displayed points. A long association tail receives a full-range/detail Manhattan view.

After analysis, insert verified figure links into your report. From `reports/my-study-report.qmd`, paths begin `../results/my-study/figures/`. Keep the guide free of another dataset's images labelled as your study.

**Your task:** choose three figures that directly address your question and state one number you will check for each.
